findings.finding: The credit agreement's $10.0m minimum-unrestricted-cash covenant is tested as of 2026-09-30, inside the window. The company held $10.075m of cash at 2026-06-30, missed the $15.0m Q2 test and needed a waiver, and carries going-concern language. A quarter-end equity raise, which can be priced and filed by 9-30, is the in-window risk.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The test date itself is 2026-09-30. Any financing done to meet it has to close by that date, and a priced offering would be filed on 8-K/424B inside the window. The compliance result is not visible until the Q3 10-Q, so only a pre-test raise can land in the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 breach and waiver were disclosed with Q2 results on 2026-08-05 (8-K items 1.01/2.04). The baseline's own falls do not include a financing day, and no prior FTCI offering reaction is in the baseline, so it gives no measured reaction on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: At about $34m of market cap, a $10m cash floor against about $10m of June cash is roughly 30% of equity value at stake. If the market fully priced a raise before 9-30, the stock would sit near a discounted offering price and the news would move nothing. Today's day of a positive MoU, with no filing, looks more like distress selling than a priced raise. The Lincoln Park ELOC ($20m, 4.5m shares registered) is capped at 20k-50k shares per regular purchase, around $1m, so it cannot fill a gap of several million dollars in one day, which leaves a discrete raise as the tool. Whether one comes is not sourced, which is why the central size is small.
findings.independence: The 2026-08-05 8-K's Limited Waiver confirms the Q2 minimum-cash breach: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828161/000119312526333770/ftci-20260804.htm. The 10-Q shows cash falling from $21.1m to $10.1m in six months and short-term debt of $22.6m: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828161/000119312526334042/ftci-20260630.htm

outside_window.finding: Disclosure of Q3 covenant compliance or a new waiver, plus going-concern language repeated in the Q3 10-Q. The report date is only the Zacks estimate, not company-announced.
Lincoln Park ELOC ($20m over 24 months, 4.56m shares registered, priced at 97% of the lowest recent prints): standing supply into any bounce, with no dated draw.
Linxon/Hitachi Energy MoU: non-binding, no volumes. It is only worth something if it turns into orders, which is not dated.
Director open-market buying at $2.46-$2.90 on 2026-08-28, above spot. It is a valuation signal with no in-window buyer.
